title: Getting Started with Node.js
body: Node.js lets developers build server-side applications with JavaScript. Start with the built-in modules and learn how requests and responses work.

title: A Practical Guide to REST APIs
body: A REST API exposes resources through predictable URLs and HTTP methods. Keep responses consistent and return meaningful status codes.

title: Why I Started Learning React
body: React makes it easier to build interactive interfaces from reusable components. Practicing small components is a good way to learn its core concepts.

title: My First API Project
body: I built a small API with routes for users and posts. The next step is adding validation and handling errors consistently.

title: Understanding HTTP Status Codes
body: Status codes communicate the outcome of a request. For example, 200 means success, 201 means a resource was created, and 404 means the resource was not found.

title: Useful JavaScript Array Methods
body: Methods such as map, filter, find, and reduce help transform and query data without writing repetitive loops.

title: How I Organize a Small Backend
body: Separating routes, controllers, and data access can make a growing project easier to understand and maintain.

title: Learning Git One Command at a Time
body: Git becomes less intimidating when you practice a small set of commands and understand what each command changes.

title: Simple Ways to Improve API Responses
body: Use a predictable response shape, validate input, and avoid returning fields clients do not need.

title: What I Learned from Debugging
body: Reading the full error message and reproducing a bug with the smallest possible example often makes debugging faster.

title: Async and Await in Practice
body: Async and await let you write promise-based code in a readable style. Remember to handle rejected promises where appropriate.

title: Choosing Clear Variable Names
body: Names that describe intent reduce the effort required to understand code. Prefer clarity over unnecessary abbreviations.

title: Filtering Data with Query Parameters
body: Query parameters are useful for filters such as status, search terms, and page numbers. Validate them before using them.

title: The Importance of Input Validation
body: Treat incoming request data as untrusted. Check required fields, data types, and allowed values before processing a request.

title: Building a Pagination Endpoint
body: Pagination helps clients request manageable slices of a collection instead of downloading every record at once.

title: Environment Variables for Local Development
body: Configuration such as port numbers can be supplied through environment variables. Avoid committing secrets to source control.

title: A Checklist Before Shipping an API
body: Test success and failure cases, validate input, choose suitable status codes, and document the expected response format.

title: Understanding Middleware
body: Middleware can inspect or modify requests and responses, perform authentication, and pass control to the next handler.

title: My Weekly Coding Routine
body: I make progress by choosing one focused topic, building a small example, and writing down what I still do not understand.

title: When to Return a 400 or 404
body: A 400 response generally indicates an invalid request, while 404 indicates that the requested resource could not be found.
